[lens/completeness][lens/scope-and-alignment][lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46` — `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` incorrectly requires both roles, denying legitimate team admins.

[lens/completeness][lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158` — calendar synchronization uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead of the booking organizer’s credentials, so attendee/admin calls can fail or update with the wrong account.

[lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation][lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74` — `!booking.attendees.some(...)` does not deduplicate the request and is a non-atomic check before `createMany`, permitting duplicate/case-variant attendees and concurrent insertion races.

[lens/architecture][lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70` — the blacklist is lowercased, but `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw address; casing bypasses the blacklist and existing-attendee check.

[lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no limit or server-side uniqueness, allowing unbounded DB/calendar work and repeated email fan-out to a victim.

[lens/intent-preservation][lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54` — authorization is followed by `attendees.createMany` without enforcing disabled-guest or seated-event capacity/reference constraints, allowing direct callers to bypass event policy.

[lens/completeness][lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26` — no status/end-time guard prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected, or completed bookings; `BookingListItem.tsx:554` also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings.

[lens/architecture] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92` — attendees commit before calendar synchronization; if synchronization fails, the API errors after mutation and retry cannot repair it because the attendee now appears existing.

[lens/architecture] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167` — notification failures are swallowed without durable retry, so the endpoint reports success although new guests may receive no invitation.

[lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168` — the mailer receives raw `guests` rather than inserted `uniqueGuests`, causing existing attendees included with a new guest to receive a fresh scheduled invitation.

[lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124` — the constructed `CalendarEvent` omits `team.members`, making the team-notification branch in `email-manager.ts:531` unreachable.

[lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525` — guest-add emails ignore host/attendee email-suppression metadata honored by adjacent booking-change notification paths.

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness][lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158` — calendar synchronization uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` instead of the booking organizer’s credentials, so attendee/admin calls can fail or update with the wrong account.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in addGuests.handler.ts, the function allows team admins, organizers, or attendees to add guests. At line 158, it uses `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` to get credentials for the EventManager. However, the calendar update should use the booking organizer's credentials (booking.user), not the current user's credentials. If an attendee or team admin (who is not the organizer) calls this endpoint, they would be using their own credentials to update the organizer's calendar, which would likely fail or update the wrong calendar. The booking already includes `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` which contains the organizer's credentials, but these are not used. This is a real bug where the wrong user's credentials are used for calendar synchronization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5` — `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no limit or server-side uniqueness, allowing unbounded DB/calendar work and repeated email fan-out to a victim.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real security concern. Looking at the schema in addGuests.schema.ts, `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` limit on array size. In the handler (addGuests.handler.ts), each guest triggers: 1) database writes to create attendees, 2) calendar API calls via `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and 3) email sends via `sendAddGuestsEmails`. While there is some filtering for duplicates against existing attendees and blacklisted emails, there's no limit on how many new guests can be added in a single request. This could allow an attacker to submit thousands of email addresses, causing unbounded database operations, calendar API calls, and email fan-out. The uniqueness check only filters against existing booking attendees, not within the submitted array itself (though the frontend has a uniqueness check, the server-side schema doesn't enforce it). This is a legitimate rate-limiting/DoS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/intent-preservation][lens/security] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:54` — authorization is followed by `attendees.createMany` without enforcing disabled-guest or seated-event capacity/reference constraints, allowing direct callers to bypass event policy.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that the addGuests handler bypasses event policy constraints like disabled-guest or seated-event capacity. Looking at the diff, the handler does check authorization (isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee) and filters out blacklisted emails and duplicate attendees. However, the code does NOT check: 1) if the event type allows guests at all (no check for eventType.disableGuests or similar), 2) if there's a maximum guest limit, 3) for seated events, whether adding guests would exceed seatsPerTimeSlot capacity. The code reads seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees for the CalendarEvent but doesn't validate against them before adding guests. This is a real authorization/validation gap - the handler allows adding guests without checking if the event type permits guests or if capacity limits would be exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/completeness][lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26` — no status/end-time guard prevents adding guests to cancelled, rejected, or completed bookings; `BookingListItem.tsx:554` also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the handler fetches the booking and checks permissions (isTeamAdminOrOwner, isOrganizer, isAttendee), but there is no validation of the booking's status field or whether the booking has already ended. The code allows adding guests to any booking regardless of whether it's cancelled, rejected, or in the past. This is a real completeness/correctness issue - the handler should validate that the booking is in an appropriate state (e.g., ACCEPTED and not yet ended) before allowing guests to be added. Similarly, BookingListItem.tsx adds the 'add_members' action to the dropdown without checking booking status or timing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92` — attendees commit before calendar synchronization; if synchronization fails, the API errors after mutation and retry cannot repair it because the attendee now appears existing.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the addGuests.handler.ts code, the flow is: 1) prisma.booking.update creates attendees (line 92-106), 2) eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called (line 161), 3) sendAddGuestsEmails is called (line 164). The finding correctly identifies that if updateCalendarAttendees fails after the database commit, the attendees are already persisted. However, examining the code more carefully: the uniqueGuests filter (lines 71-75) checks against booking.attendees which was fetched at the start, not the updated list. If a retry happens, the new guests would already be in the database and would be filtered out by the uniqueGuests check, causing 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error. This is a real atomicity/consistency issue - the database mutation happens before external calendar sync, and there's no rollback mechanism if calendar sync fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167` — notification failures are swallowed without durable retry, so the endpoint reports success although new guests may receive no invitation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in addGuests.handler.ts lines 167-170, the sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in a try-catch that only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and then continues to return success. This means if email sending fails, the API returns {message: 'Guests added'} even though guests may not have received their invitation emails. This is a real correctness issue - the endpoint reports success when a critical part of the operation (notifying guests) may have failed, with no retry mechanism or error propagation to the caller.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent 'evt' is constructed without a 'team' property. In email-manager.ts:531, the sendAddGuestsEmails function checks 'if (calendarEvent.team?.members)' to send emails to team members. Since 'evt' doesn't include 'team.members', this branch will never execute, meaning team members won't receive notification emails when guests are added. This is a real bug - the code structure in sendAddGuestsEmails expects team.members to be populated for team bookings, but the handler doesn't populate it.
